descs: The Lastwater's lower bank, reed and willow, the current slowing as it feels Longford coming.
briefs: The lower bank, reed and willow.

spots.name: The North Reed
spots.desc: Reeds close overhead, cut through by a path too straight to be a deer-track. Someone walks this often, and lately in a hurry.

actions.label: brace a shortcut through the thin reeds
fx: You shoulder through where the reeds grow thinnest — not a path yet, only ground that will be one, the way a warden reads it.

actions.label: count how many pass this way
fx: More than a footpath ought to see and fewer than the toll-board would like. Someone's still finding reasons to come this way instead.

spots.name: Ferrier's Bend
spots.desc: The bank curves hard here, and the current with it. North the reed-path climbs toward Pennywell; the toll camp's smoke is already visible south, thin and steady.
spots.brief: The bend, Pennywell north, smoke south.

actions.label: get your bearings

spots.name: The Osier Stand
spots.desc: Willow cut for basket-work, most of it years unharvested. Whoever tended this stand hasn't had the toll-free time to since the rail went up.

actions.label: cut a length of willow
fx: You cut clean, the way someone taught you once. A scout notices what a place used to be for.

actions.label: count the unharvested years
fx: Three seasons of growth, maybe four, gone to waste on a stand somebody used to work every year without fail. The toll ate the time before it ate anything else.

spots.name: The Hedge Crossing
spots.desc: A gap worn through a boundary hedge, the Shieldings' open plain visible beyond it. East the ground softens toward the water.
spots.brief: A gap in the hedge, the plain beyond.

actions.label: get your bearings

spots.name: The Still Reach
spots.desc: The current dies here, backed up behind something under the surface. Whatever it is, the water's given up trying to move it.
spots.brief: Dead water, backed up on something.

actions.label: read what's snagged the current
fx: A scout's eye picks out what the current can't move: an old skiff timber, waterlogged black, wedged crosswise on the bar. Someone's boat, once.

actions.label: watch the dead water a while
fx: Nothing surfaces. Nothing needs to. The water's made its peace with whatever it's carrying and isn't in any hurry to say what.

spots.name: The Drowned Milestone
spots.desc: A Crown milepost, half-sunk, the number worn past reading. It marked a distance to somewhere that mattered enough to measure, once.

actions.label: read what's left of the marker
fx: Old figures, older than the House of the Reeve. This road was measured before there was a Crown to measure it for.

actions.label: trace the stone's worn shape by hand
fx: Whatever it once said is gone to touch as much as sight. Someone still comes by often enough to keep the moss from finishing the job.

spots.name: Heron's Watch
spots.desc: A heron works the shallows here, unbothered by toll or traveler. It has the better claim to the crossing than anyone charging for it.

actions.label: watch the heron work
fx: It spears something small and silver, unhurried, and goes back to standing on one leg like the toll rail downstream is somebody else's problem. It's not wrong.

spots.name: The Old Weir
spots.desc: A fish-weir, stones stacked with care generations ago, still mostly whole. Nobody has tended it since the fish stopped being worth the walk to check.

actions.label: read how the weir was built
fx: The coursing's older than any technique taught now — laid by hands that expected the weir to outlast them, and it has, by generations.

actions.label: walk the weir's spine
fx: The stones hold underfoot, dry-fitted so tight the river's had a hundred years to find a gap and hasn't.

spots.name: The Reed Maze
spots.desc: Channels through the reeds, none of them obviously the way through. Something has trampled a path anyway, low and deliberate.

actions.label: follow the trampled channel
fx: The trample runs low and wide, dragging more than walking. Whatever made it isn't far — Cutter's Hollow sits just east, and the smell agrees with you.

actions.label: pick a channel and commit to it
fx: It dead-ends in reed and mud like the last three. Every channel here looks like a decision until you're standing in it.

spots.name: Cutter's Hollow
spots.desc: A hollow in the bank, scored with claw-marks at shoulder height. Whatever cut them is not visible, and the smell says it hasn't gone far.
spots.brief: A clawed hollow in the bank.

actions.label: look for what made the marks
fx: The marks go back further than the light reaches, deeper into the bank than a hollow this size ought to allow. Something dug this out on purpose.

spots.name: The Long Shallows
spots.desc: The river spreads thin and slow, shallow enough in a dry season to walk without the ford at all — which is likely why the toll camp sits where it does, and not here.

actions.label: wade the shallows, unwatched
fx: You wade it dry-season shallow, boots in hand, and stand on the far bank without a toll-man ever turning your way. Not everyone crossing here needs to know about this.

actions.label: wade in a few steps, no further
fx: Ankle-deep and clear enough to see the bottom. Shallow, certainly — how far it stays that way is a question for someone willing to keep walking.

spots.name: Bramble Bank
spots.desc: A bramble thicket grown up around what might once have been a fisherman's plot. Smoke rises thin from somewhere inside it, banked low on purpose.
spots.brief: A bramble thicket, smoke banked low.

actions.label: read the banked-low smoke
fx: Smoke banked that low isn't carelessness. Someone in there doesn't want to be found by a casual glance — and is watching you notice it anyway.

actions.label: listen at the brambles a moment
fx: No voices, just the small sounds of someone keeping still on purpose. Whoever's in there has had practice not being spoken to.

spots.name: The Gravel Bar
spots.desc: A spit of gravel the river hasn't decided whether to keep. Old coin washes up here sometimes, dropped by ferrymen going back further than Nan's grandmother.
spots.brief: A gravel spit, old coin in it sometimes.

actions.label: sift the gravel a while longer
fx: Nothing else turns up but river-smoothed stone, and a sense of how many hands have done exactly this before yours.

spots.name: The Willow Steps
spots.desc: Roots grown into something like stairs, down to the water. Someone has used this crossing so long the willow itself remembers the shape of it.

actions.label: test the willow-steps
fx: The roots hold your weight without a creak, worn smooth by feet that trusted them long before yours did.

spots.name: The South Path
spots.desc: The reed-path opens onto packed gravel, and Longford's rooftops show through the willows south. The toll camp's smoke is close now, close enough to smell the fires.
spots.brief: The path opens; Longford is close.

actions.label: get your bearings

spots.name: Ashwood Landing
spots.desc: A stand of old ash trees, and under them a chapel roof gone green with moss. A path worn by pilgrims' feet, not toll-men's, leads to its door.
spots.brief: Old ash trees, a mossy chapel roof.

actions.label: count the rings in the old stumps
fx: The ash grove is older than the chapel under it by generations, near as a rough count can tell. Someone built a chapel to what was already here, not the other way round.

actions.label: stand a moment under the ash
fx: The canopy's thick enough to quiet the toll camp entirely. Whoever built the chapel here knew what the trees were worth before they knew what the saint was.

vars.NAME: Cutter's Hollow
vars.SIGN: The scat is fresher than the claw-marks, and both are fresh.

vars.NAME: the Bramble Hide
vars.SIGN: A Free Company knife, well-kept, hangs by the door — the one thing here not mended twice over.
vars.VOICE: Company doesn't own this bank. Company doesn't want to. I just watch, and I watch for coin.

vars.NAME: the Broken Oar Chapel
vars.SIGN: A ferryman's oar, broken, is nailed above the door — an old offering for an old crossing.

lf_old_coin.name: an old ferry-penny
lf_old_coin.hint: worn past any king's face; a keepsake, older than the toll

lf_tollman.name: a toll-man
lf_tollman.desc: One of Voss's hired men, sent out to remind the wilderness who's collecting now.
onDeath: The toll-man goes down, and won't be reporting back to the captain tonight.
